title: Warming and cooling contrasts in corrected community change were uncertain in four US trawl samples in 1982-2019
abstract: We tested whether warming and cooling gave different amounts of annual community change at equal temperature-change magnitude. We used fixed-stratum trawl records from the eastern Bering Sea and Northeast US fall surveys in 1982-2019. A published measure fixes haul effort and corrects finite-sample noise under independent sampling assumptions. Four region-period models control change magnitude and linear year. Warming-minus-cooling contrasts at one degree range from -4.71 to +0.25 squared detection-probability units. All four adjusted intervals include zero. Covariance, uncorrected-distance and survey-transition checks give the same broad result. This does not show equal responses. Short series, coarse surface temperature, gear and detection limit inference. We do not estimate causal climate effects, heatwaves or pollution. The package gives data, raw source hashes, code, a figure and independent numerical checks.

display.caption: Annual corrected community change and warming-minus-cooling model contrasts. All four adjusted intervals include zero. Positive contrast values mean more predicted change after warming at equal magnitude. The late Northeast one-degree warming prediction extends above the observed 0.900 C maximum.

citations.reason: Verified source of incidence, design, SST evidence, correction and code. We extend the absolute-change model with a signed-change contrast on the same observations.
Original source of retained strata, incidence and climate build code, inherited via the corrected-distance publication.
